```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false


import {vl} from "@vega/vega-lite-api"
import { aq, op } from "@uwdata/arquero"
import {Plot} from "@mkfreeman/plot-tooltip"
import {addTooltips} from "@mkfreeman/plot-tooltip"


vg = require('vega-lite')

// references to images stored in data folder for each response variable
imageURL_invert = FileAttachment("/data/invert 2.png").url()
imageURL_peri = FileAttachment("/data/periphyton.png").url()
imageURL_gravel = FileAttachment("/data/gravel.png").url() 
imageURL_parr = FileAttachment("/data/parr_len.png").url()
imageURL_salmon = FileAttachment("/data/NOAA_atlantic_salmon.png").url()
imageURL_parrgrow = FileAttachment("/data/parr_grow.png").url()

//** imageURL_response = FileAttachment("/data/response_file_name.png").url() 


// function to convert all predictions that are negative to 0
function negativetozero(equation) { 
  return op.bin(equation, 0, op.greatest(equation), 0.0001)
}

// colour scheme for bars
myColours = ["#325D88", "#1F78B4"]
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| panel: fill

// prediction functions
function invertbiomass(peri) { //returns predicted invert based on 
  return negativetozero(1.133+5.50*peri) //numbers here are intercept and slope
}

function peribiomass(EPT) {
  return negativetozero(0.01 + 0.08*EPT) 
}

// example adding predicitons for parr 
//** function parrbiomass(variable1) {
//**   return negativetozero(0.22 + 0.74*variable1) 
//** }

// error bar functions
function inverthigh(peri) {
  return negativetozero(1.133+0.19+(5.50+1.89)*peri)
}

function invertlow(peri) {
  return negativetozero(1.133-0.19+(5.50-1.89)*peri)
}

function perihigh(EPT) {
  return negativetozero((0.01+0.02)  + (0.08+0.02)*EPT) 
}

function perilow(EPT) {
  return negativetozero((0.01-0.02) + (0.08-0.02)*EPT) 
}

// example adding error bars for parr 
//** function parrhigh(variable1) {
//**   return negativetozero((0.22+0.003) + (0.74+0.2)*variable1) 
//** }

//** function parrlow(variable1) {
//**   return negativetozero((0.22-0.003) + (0.74-0.2)*variable1) 
//** }


// function that takes input from sliders and creates prediction of each response variable based on functions above
function myFunction(peri,
                    //** parr,
                    EPT) { 
  return aq.table({
  'peri': [peri,
           //** peri,
           peri], // repeat for each input (so if adding parr you would add the third rep of each peri and EPT
  'EPT': [EPT,
          //** EPT,
          EPT],
  //** 'variable1': [variable1, variable1, variable1],
  'response_type': ["Predicted invertebrate density (g/m²)", 
                    "Predicted periphyton density (μg/cm²)",
                    //** "Predicted parr density (g m⁻²)"
                    ],
  'response_predict': [invertbiomass(peri), // order same as response type
                      peribiomass(EPT),
                      //** parrbiomass(variable1)
                      ],
  'response_errorhigh': [inverthigh(peri), // order same as response type
                        perihigh(EPT),
                      //** parrhigh(variable1)
                        ],
  'response_errorlow': [invertlow(peri), // order same as response type
                        perilow(EPT),
                      //** parrlow(variable1)
                        ]
  })
}

// create the table
predictions_ps = myFunction(peri, 
                            EPT,
                            //** parr,
                            ) 


// create a table that stores the image paths
images = aq.table({
  'response_type': ["Predicted invertebrate density (g/m²)",
                    "Predicted periphyton density (μg/cm²)",
                    //** "Predicted parr density (g m⁻²)",
                    ],
  'image_path': [imageURL_invert, //order these to match  ordered response variables (response_type)
                  imageURL_peri
                  //** imageURL_parr,
                  ] 
})


// create the bar plot based on predictions_ps
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.max(width, 250),
  height: Math.floor(0.25 * width),
  marginLeft: 0,
  marginRight: 0,
  marginBottom: 30,
  color: {range: myColours,
  legend: false},
  y: {domain: [0,8], axis: null},
  x: {label: null, domain: ["Predicted invertebrate density (g/m²)", 
                            "Predicted periphyton density (μg/cm²)",
                            //** "Predicted parr density (g m⁻²) "
                            ]},
  
  // create bar graph
  marks:[
    Plot.axisX({fontSize: Math.max(16, width / 80)}), 
    Plot.barY(predictions_ps,
     {x: "response_type",
     y: "response_predict",
     fill: "response_type"}), 
    
     // write out predicted value
    Plot.text(predictions_ps, {x: "response_type", y: "response_predict", text: "response_predict", dy: -7, dx: -width/8, lineAnchor: "bottom", fontSize: Math.max(16, width / 80)}), 
    
    // add error bars
    Plot.ruleX(predictions_ps, {x: "response_type", y1: 'response_errorlow', y2: 'response_errorhigh', strokeWidth: 3}) 
   ]
})

// add images below each bar
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.max(width, 550),
  height: Math.floor(0.08 * width),
  marginLeft: 0,
  marginRight: 0,
  colour: {legend: false},
  y: {domain: [0,0], axis: null},
  x: {label: "Response type", axis: null, fontSize: 22, 
      domain: ["Predicted invertebrate density (g/m²)", // match this order to above
              "Predicted periphyton density (μg/cm²)",
               //** "Predicted parr density (g m⁻²) "
               ]},
  marks:[
    Plot.image(images, 
      {x: "response_type",
      y: [0, 0, 0, 0],
      src: "image_path",
      width: 150,
      axis: null
      })
   ]
})


```
 
\

| <u><b>Desciption of models and variables:</b></u> 

| A suite of predictor variables, measured in field, were assessed for their correlation to invertebrate and periphyton biomass, using general linear models (GLMs) compared using Akaike’s Information Criterion corrected for small sample sizes. The variables we included in the final models are represented as sliders above.  

| <b>Sliders</b>: 

| Periphyton density (μg cm⁻²): The density of algae, microbes, bacteria, and detritus attached to substrate. 

| Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera density (g m⁻²): The density of  invertebrates on the families Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, and Trichoptera. 

| <b>Predicted values</b>: 

| Invertebrate density (g cm⁻²): The density of all invertebrates predicted to occur based on GLMs.

| Periphyton density (μg cm⁻²): The density of algae, microbes, bacteria, and detritus attached to substrate, predicted to occur based on GLMs.

## Parr length and growth responses

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false

// Start with "invert" as the default active slider
viewof active_slider = Inputs.radio(["alkalinity", "conduct", "invert_bio"], {
  value: "alkalinity"
})
```

Click a variable to activate. 

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| panel: input
//| layout-ncol: 3

// sliders for predictor variables

// Stream alkalinity
viewof alkalinity = {
  const form = Inputs.range(
  [10, 50], 
  {value: 25, step: 40/100, label: "Alkalinity (mg/L):"}
);
  form.range.style.cssText += "accent-color: #1f78b4; width: 110%";
  form.number.style.cssText += "color: #031D5E; background-color: #E4F3F7; border: 1px solid #031D5E; border-radius: 3px; text-align: right; padding: none";
  
  const label = form.querySelector("label");
  label.style.cssText += "width: 100%; margin-top: 10px";

  const wrapper = html`<div style="
    padding: 10px; 
    border-radius: 7px; 
    cursor: pointer;
    transition: opacity 0.2s;
    opacity: ${active_slider === "alkalinity" ? "1" : "0.4"};
  "></div>`;
  
  wrapper.appendChild(form);

  // Set initial value
  wrapper.value = form.value;

  form.addEventListener("input", (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation(); // Stop the inner event loop
    wrapper.value = form.value; // Sync the value
    wrapper.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); // Notify Observable
  });
  
  // Disable internal inputs if this source isn't active
  form.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(inp => {
    inp.disabled = (active_slider !== "alkalinity");
  });

  // Catch clicks on a disabled slider to activate it
  wrapper.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
    if (active_slider !== "alkalinity") {
      // Update the master controller cell
      viewof active_slider.value = "alkalinity";
      viewof active_slider.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
    }
  });
  
  return wrapper;

}

// Stream conductivity
viewof conduct = {
  const form = Inputs.range(
  [10, 50], 
  {value: 30, step: 40/100, label: "Conductivity (µS/cm):"}
);
  form.range.style.cssText += "accent-color: #1f78b4; width: 110%";
  form.number.style.cssText += "color: #031D5E; background-color: #E4F3F7; border: 1px solid #031D5E; border-radius: 3px; text-align: right; padding: none";
  
  const label = form.querySelector("label");
  label.style.cssText += "width: 100%; margin-top: 10px";

  // Dynamically disable based on our toggle state
  const wrapper = html`<div style="
    padding: 6px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.2s;
    opacity: ${active_slider === "conduct" ? "1" : "0.4"};
  "></div>`;
  
  wrapper.appendChild(form);
  wrapper.value = form.value;

  form.addEventListener("input", (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    wrapper.value = form.value;
    wrapper.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  });
  
  form.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(inp => inp.disabled = (active_slider !== "conduct"));
  
  //Catch clicks on a disabled slider to activate it
  wrapper.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
    if (active_slider !== "conduct") {
      // Update the master controller cell
      viewof active_slider.value = "conduct";
      viewof active_slider.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
    }
  });
  
  return wrapper;
}



//invert biomass

viewof invert_bio = {  //name slider
  const form = Inputs.range(
  [0, 20],  // put minimum values and maximum
  {value: 1, // starting value
   step: 20/1000, // amount able to step by
   label: "Invertebrate biomass (g):"} // label above slider
);  // below is all styling
  form.range.style.cssText += "accent-color: #1f78b4; width: 110%";
  form.number.style.cssText += "color: #031D5E; background-color: #E4F3F7; border: 1px solid #031D5E; border-radius: 3px; text-align: right; padding: none";
    
  const label = form.querySelector("label");
  label.style.cssText += "width: 100%";

  // Dynamically disable based on our toggle state
  const wrapper = html`<div style="
    padding: 6px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.2s;
    opacity: ${active_slider === "invert_bio" ? "1" : "0.4"};
  "></div>`;
  
  wrapper.appendChild(form);
  wrapper.value = form.value;

  form.addEventListener("input", (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    wrapper.value = form.value;
    wrapper.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  });
  
  form.querySelectorAll("input").forEach(inp => inp.disabled = (active_slider !== "invert_bio"));
  
  //Catch clicks on a disabled slider to activate it
  wrapper.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
    if (active_slider !== "invert_bio") {
      // Update the master controller cell
      viewof active_slider.value = "invert_bio";
      viewof active_slider.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
    }
  });
  
  return wrapper;
  
}

```



```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| panel: fill

// prediction functions

// parr length model(s)
function parrlenin(invert_bio) {
  return negativetozero(85.0179+(0.7332)*invert_bio); 
}

function parrlenco(conduct) {
  return negativetozero(78.2348+(0.4124)*conduct); 
}

// parr growth rate model(s)
function parrgrowal(alkalinity) {
  return negativetozero(8.1524+(0.6794)*alkalinity); 
}

function parrgrowco(conduct) {
  return negativetozero(10.1007+(0.4872)*conduct); 
}

// error bar functions

//high
function parrlenin_high(invert_bio) {
  return negativetozero((85.0179+2.2681)+(0.7332+0.2326)*invert_bio); 
}

function parrlenco_high(conduct) {
  return negativetozero((78.2348+5.6265)+(0.4124+0.1806)*conduct); 
}

function parrgrowal_high(alkalinity) {
  return negativetozero((8.1524+5.4389)+(0.6794+0.2165)*alkalinity);
}

function parrgrowco_high(conduct) {
  return negativetozero((10.1007+5.0549)+(0.4872+0.1623)*conduct); 
}

//low
function parrlenin_low(invert_bio) {
  return negativetozero((85.0179-2.2681)+(0.7332-0.2326)*invert_bio); 
}

function parrlenco_low(conduct) {
  return negativetozero((78.2348-5.6265)+(0.4124-0.1806)*conduct); 
}

function parrgrowal_low(alkalinity) {
  return negativetozero((8.1524-5.4389)+(0.6794-0.2165)*alkalinity);
}

function parrgrowco_low(conduct) {
  return negativetozero((10.1007-5.0549)+(0.4872-0.1623)*conduct); 
}

// function that takes input from sliders and creates prediction of each response variable based on above functions
// put into toggle output so that when either slider is seleceted, the other turns off

function parrFunction1(invert_bio, conduct, alkalinity) {
  return aq.table({
  'invert_bio': [invert_bio, invert_bio], // repeat for each value predicting
  'conduct': [conduct, conduct],
  'alkalinity':[alkalinity, alkalinity],
  'response_type': ["Salmon parr growth rate (mm/yr)",
                      "Salmon parr length (mm)"
                    ], // ordered alphabetically
                      
  'response_predict': [parrgrowco(conduct),
                        parrlenco(conduct)
                      ],
  'response_predict_label': [parrgrowco(conduct),
                        parrlenco(conduct)
                      ],
  'response_errorhigh': [parrgrowco_high(conduct), // order same as response type
                        parrlenco_high(conduct),
                      //** parrhigh(variable1)
                        ],
  'response_errorlow': [parrgrowco_low(conduct), // order same as response type
                        parrlenco_low(conduct),
                      //** parrlow(variable1)
                        ]
  })
}

function parrFunction2(invert_bio, conduct, alkalinity) {
  return aq.table({
  'invert_bio': [invert_bio, invert_bio], // repeat for each value predicting
  'conduct': [conduct, conduct],
  'alkalinity':[alkalinity, alkalinity],
  'response_type': ["Salmon parr growth rate (mm/yr)",
                      "Salmon parr length (mm)"
                    ], // ordered alphabetically
                      
  'response_predict': [parrgrowal(alkalinity),
                        parrlenin(invert_bio)
                      ],
  'response_predict_label': [parrgrowal(alkalinity),
                        parrlenin(invert_bio)
                      ],
  'response_errorhigh': [parrgrowal_high(alkalinity), // order same as response type
                        parrlenin_high(invert_bio),
                      //** parrhigh(variable1)
                        ],
  'response_errorlow': [parrgrowal_low(alkalinity), // order same as response type
                        parrlenin_low(invert_bio),
                      //** parrlow(variable1)
                        ]
  })
}

// create the table
predictions_parr1 = parrFunction1(invert_bio, conduct, alkalinity)
predictions_parr2 = parrFunction2(invert_bio, conduct, alkalinity)

active_data = {
  if (active_slider === "conduct") {
    // Calculate with Table A using the active invert_bio variable
    return predictions_parr1;
  } else {
    // Fallback default dataset
    return predictions_parr2;
  }
}



// create a tables that stores the image paths
image_parrlen = aq.table({ //split gravel and salmon so I could specify the image sizes better
  'response_type': ["Salmon parr length (mm)"
                    ], 
  'image_path': [imageURL_parr
                  ] 
})

image_parrgrow = aq.table({ 
  'response_type': ["Salmon parr growth rate (mm/yr)",
                    ],
  'image_path': [imageURL_parrgrow
                  ] 
})

// create the bar plot based on predictions_ps
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.max(width, 250),
  height: Math.floor(0.25 * width),
  marginLeft: 0,
  marginRight: 0,
  marginBottom: 30,
  color: {range: myColours,
  legend: false},
  y: {domain: [0, 200], label: null},
  x: {label: null},
  marks:[
    Plot.axisX({fontSize: Math.max(16, width / 80), marginBottom: 40}),
    Plot.barY(active_data,
     {x: "response_type",
     y: "response_predict",
     fill: "response_type"}), // create bar graph
    Plot.text(active_data, {x: "response_type", y: "response_predict", text: "response_predict_label", dy: -7, dx: -width/8, lineAnchor: "bottom", fontSize: Math.max(16, width / 80)}), 
    
    // add error bars
    Plot.ruleX(active_data, {x: "response_type", y1: 'response_errorlow', y2: 'response_errorhigh', strokeWidth: 3}) 
   ]
})

// add images below each bar
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.max(width, 550),
  height: Math.floor(0.085 * width),
  marginTop: 10,
  marginLeft: 0,
  marginRight: 0,
  colour: {legend: false},
  y: {domain: [0,0], axis: null},
  x: {label: "Response type", axis: null, fontSize: 22},
  marks:[
    Plot.image(image_parrgrow, 
      {x: "response_type",
      y: [0, 0],
      src: "image_path",
      width: width/8,
      axis: null
      }),
    Plot.image(image_parrlen, 
      {x: "response_type",
      y: [0, 0],
      src: "image_path",
      width: 200,
      axis: null
      })
   ]
})

```

| <u><b>Desciption of models and variables:</b></u> 

| A suite of predictor variables, measured in field, were assessed for their correlation to salmon parr growth rate and length, using general linear models (GLMs). The variables with significant correlation to salmon parr growth rate and length are represented as sliders above.  

| <b>Sliders</b>: 

| Alkalinity (mg/L): ...

| Conductivity (µS/cm): .... 

| Invertebrate density (g m⁻²): .... 

| <b>Predicted values</b>: 

| Salmon parr growth rate (mm/yr): The growth rate of salmon parr, difference between lengths of salmon parr aged 2 year and 1 year over time (1 year),  predicted to occur based on alklainity or conductivity.

|   Salmon parr growth rate = (8.1524±5.4389)+(0.6794±0.2165)*alkalinity

|   Salmon parr growth rate = (10.1007±5.0549)+(0.4872±0.1623)*conductivity

| Salmon parr length (mm): The length of salmon parr predicted to occur based on conductivity or invertebrate biomass.

|   Salmon parr length = (85.0179±2.2681)+(0.7332±0.2326)*invertebrate biomass

|   Salmon parr length = (78.2348±5.6265)+(0.4124±0.1806)*conductivity


| <b>Citation:</b> ...

```{ojs}
}

// Fish length
viewof fish = {
  const form = Inputs.range(
  [40, 200], 
  {value: 100, step: (200-40)/100, label: "Fish length (cm):"}
);
  form.range.style.cssText += "accent-color: #1f78b4; width: 110%";
  form.number.style.cssText += "color: #031D5E; background-color: #E4F3F7; border: 1px solid #031D5E; border-radius: 3px; text-align: right; padding: none";
  
  const label = form.querySelector("label");
  label.style.cssText += "width: 100%; margin-top: 10px";

  return form;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| panel: fill

// prediction functions

// gravel model
function gravelsize(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav) {
  return (2000 * op.pow(0.05, (3 / 5)) * op.pow((DIS_AV_CMS / swidth), (3 / 5)) * op.pow(sgr_dk_rav/1000, (7 / 10)) / (650 * 0.04)) * 1000 ;
}



// ideal fish size as exponential curve, where 16 is ideal for 0.1 m fish and 64 is ideal for 2m fish

function idealsize(fish) {
  return 109 * (op.pow(1.26, fish/100) - 1)
}

// spawning suitability that responds to fish length
function spawningprob(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav, fish) {
  if(16 <= gravelsize(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav) <=64) {
  return op.exp((-1/2) * (op.pow((gravelsize(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav) - idealsize(fish))/8, 2)));
  } else {
  return 0
  }
}



// function that takes input from sliders and creates prediction of each response variable based on above functions

function gravelFunction(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav, fish) {
  return aq.table({
  'DIS_AV_CMS': [DIS_AV_CMS, DIS_AV_CMS], // repeat for each value predicting
  'swidth': [swidth, swidth],
  'sgr_dk_rav':[sgr_dk_rav, sgr_dk_rav],
  'fish': [fish, fish],
  'response_type': ["Predicted gravel size (D50; mm)", 
                    "Suitability of predicted gravel size for \nspawning by salmon of given length" //not sure what this variable will be yet
                    ], // ordered alphabetically
                      
  'response_predict': [gravelsize(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav),
                        spawningprob(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav, fish)*2000
                      ],
  'response_predict_label': [gravelsize(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav),
                        spawningprob(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav, fish)
                      ]
  })
}

// create the table
predictions_gravel = gravelFunction(DIS_AV_CMS, swidth, sgr_dk_rav, fish)

  'response_type': ["Gravel size D50 (m)"

})
```

| <u><b>Desciption of models and variables:</b></u> 

| Gravel size is important to the Atlantic Salmon spawning; too fine or too coarse, and the salmon will either not spawn or have poor egg survival (Purchase 2018). 

| <b>D50 Gravel size:</b> was predicted based on the following calculations (Wilkins & Snyder 2011)
| 
| D50 = 𝛕<sub>b</sub> / (𝛒<sub>s</sub> - 𝛒) * g * 𝛕<sup>* </sup>
| 
| <u>Parameters:</u>
| 𝛕<sub>b</sub> = 𝛒 * g * n<sup>3/5</sup> * [Q/W]<sup>3/5</sup> * S<sup>7/10</sup>
| 𝛒 = density of water = 1000 kg/m<sup>3</sup>
| g = acceleration by gravity = 9.80665 m/s<sup>2</sup>
| n = channel roughness coefficient = 0.05 as within estimates for gravel, cobble and boulder rivers (Aldridge & Garrett, 1973; Barnes, 1967)
| 𝛒<sub>s</sub> = sediment density = 2650 kg/m<sup>3</sup>
| 𝛕<sup>*</sup>  =  Shields parameter = 0.04 a median estimate of gravel-bed rivers by Mueller et al. (2005) and Wilkins & Snyder (2011)
| 
| <u>Variables to retreive from HydroSHEDs:</u>
| S = channel gradient, Calculated as the ratio between the elevation drop within the river reach (i.e. the difference between min. and max. elevation along the reach) and the length of the reach.
| Q = Discharge (m<sup>3</sup>/s), Average long-term discharge estimate for river reach, in cubic meters per second.
| W = channel width (m), Calculated as the surface river area of the river reach segment divided by length of the river reach segment.
|  
| 
| <b>Spawning suitability:</b> in predicted gravel size  for fish of chosen length (m) calculated using the following equation:
| 
| Suitability = e<sup>((-1/2) * ((D50 - ideal.fish.gravel)/8)<sup>2</sup>)</sup>
| 
| Ideal.fish.gravel = 109 * (1.26<sup>fish.length</sup> - 1)
| 
| This equation associates a higher probability of spawning in larger gravel for longer fish, and a higher probability of spawning in smaller gravel for smaller fish.  
| Assumes the ideal spawning gravel for a fish of 2m is 64 mm,  for a fish of 1 m is 32 mm, for a fish of 0 m is 16 mm etc, with a bell shaped distribution of suitability around the ideal gravel size with a standard deviation of 8. If D50 is lower than 16 or higher than 64, the suitability is 0.
|
| <b> Citations: </b>
|  
| Aldridge, B. N., & Garrett, J. M. (1973). Roughness coefficients for stream channels in Arizona (p. 87). U.S. Geological Survey.
| Barnes, H. H. Jr. (1967). Roughness characteristics of natural channels (U.S. Geological Survey Water-Supply Paper 1849, p. 213). U.S. Geological Survey. 
| Lehner, B., & Grill, G. (2013). Global river hydrography and network routing: Baseline data and new approaches to study the world’s large river systems. Hydrological Processes, 27(15), 2171– 2186. https://doi.org/10.1002/hyp.9740 
| Linke, S., Lehner, B., Ouellet Dallaire, C., Ariwi, J., Grill, G., Anand, M., Beames, P., Burchard-Levine, V., Maxwell, S., Moidu, H., Tan, F., & Thieme, M. (2019). Global hydro-environmental sub-basin and river reach characteristics at high spatial resolution. Scientific Data, 6(1), 283. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-019-0300-6  
| Mueller, E. R., Pitlick, J., & Nelson, J. M. (2005). Variation in the reference Shields stress for bed load transport in gravel-bed streams and rivers. Water Resources Research, 41(4). https://doi.org/10.1029/2004WR003692
| Purchase, C. P. (2026). A systematic review on the effectiveness of salmonid spawning habitat improvements, and recommendations to potentially increase productivity of depressed Newfoundland Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) populations. EcoEvoRxiv. https://doi.org/10.32942/X2V673
| Wilkins, B. C., & Snyder, N. P. (2011). Geomorphic comparison of two Atlantic coastal rivers: Toward on understanding of physical controls on Atlantic salmon habitat. River Research and Applications, 27(2), 135–156. https://doi.org/10.1002/rra.1343
